title: Sneaker reselling: when it pays and when it just sits
description: Reselling sneakers looks like easy money, but nine out of ten pairs end up in your closet. How to spot a pair worth flipping — and when to just wear them.
excerpt: Everyone knows someone who made $200 on one pair. Nobody talks about the four pairs under his bed from last year.
content:
Sneaker reselling sounds like the easiest business on earth: buy at $160, sell at $320. The reality is that most pairs drop below retail within weeks of the release, and you either eat the loss or wear them — which, honestly, is the better outcome.

## What actually holds value

Three things keep prices up: a small production run, a real story behind the shoe, and sizes people actually wear. A collab capped at a few thousand pairs holds. A general restock of a model sitting in every store never does. Watch sizes too — US 9 and 10 sell worst because they're produced most. Edge sizes hold price better, they just move slower.

## Do the whole math, not the spread

Platforms take 8–12% of the sale price, then add payment fees and shipping. Buy at $160, sell at $200, and you're left with maybe $15 for two hours of work. Add the risk of a failed authentication and a return, and you'll see why only spreads above 40% are worth touching.

## When to just wear them

If you like the pair and paid retail, stop overthinking it and wear them. Sneakers only hold value deadstock — the moment they touch pavement you're back in the regular market. Decide at checkout which bucket the pair belongs to, and don't leave it in limbo for months.
